title: Code and data release for "When a compliance score rewards the wrong adjustment: auditing grid-code forecast assessment in China's wind sector"
description:
Code and data for the manuscript When a compliance score rewards the wrong adjustment: auditing grid-code forecast assessment in China's wind sector. The archive documents three years of an automated code-editing loop on a provincial Chinese wind fleet whose only acceptance criterion was the grid-code compliance score: 106 floored runs (5,360 planned iterations, 5,200 executed, 1,202 accepted code edits), 32 holdout runs, and 32 runs with installed capacity as the objective denominator, 170 runs in total. The score rose by 1.02 points; the gain survived both holdout designs and transfer to farms outside each pipeline's search set, but not a change of loss: capacity-normalised squared error and capacity-normalised absolute error both deteriorated on identical predictions.

Three exercises locate the cause: an exact decomposition attributes +1.44 of the +0.90-point pair-level change to intervals below 20% of installed capacity and -0.54 to the rest; re-running the loop with installed capacity as the objective denominator collapses its gain from 1.09 to 0.05 points; and one multiplicative constant gains 4.19 points where sixty iterations of code search gained 1.10.

The deposit contains the artefacts of 138 runs (the 106 floored and the 32 capacity-denominator runs), the result tables behind Tables 1-8, the scripts that produce every printed number and Figures 1-5, and a verification script that re-checks 142 printed values. The 32 holdout runs are represented by their split manifest and per-run results.

The metered output and the issued day-ahead forecast series are confidential under a data-sharing agreement with the provincial system operator and are not included; no de-identified sample is available and requests for access cannot be granted.

Code is released under the MIT licence; result tables and run artefacts are released under CC BY 4.0.
